objective: Phase 4 follow-up: decide the BIL idle-cash reserve candidate from reports/cash_reserve_study.json, which the pre-registered return_enhancer hard gate rejected by a 1bp drawdown margin despite better Sharpe and CAGR in both windows.
source_evidence: reports/cash_reserve_study.json, decision_bil: reject, gates_bil.early_2020_2022.max_drawdown_not_worse: false (all other checks true in both windows).
why_not_risk_reducer: The Phase 4 plan text suggested judging this under the risk_reducer objective class (backtest/promotion.py), but that class is shaped for a candidate trading CAGR away for less drawdown (a hedge, a vol overlay) — it requires pre-declaring max_cagr_cost_pp (a cost the study must be willing to pay). BIL's actual result is the opposite shape: CAGR and Sharpe both improve in both windows; the only failure is a 1bp-worse drawdown in one window. Forcing this into risk_reducer's framework would mean inventing a cost-budget for a candidate that isn't costing anything, which is not what that objective class is for. It also was not the objective class cash_reserve_study.py pre-registered, and retroactively picking a different class after seeing a result that doesn't fit the first one is exactly the after-the-fact conditioning this project's own research-discipline rules (AGENTS.md) exist to prevent.
reasoning: This reads as a razor's-edge hard-gate near-miss with genuinely strong other-axis evidence, the same pattern already used to justify three other 2x-lab experiment-tier launches this session (MOM_LS breadth, TSMOM FXE drop, the averaging-down restoration exemption): better Sharpe AND better CAGR in both screening windows, with the only blemish a 1bp drawdown difference (-0.1254 vs -0.1253) in one window that is not economically distinguishable from noise for a near-zero-duration T-bill substitute for idle cash. The pre-registered return_enhancer gate's zero-tolerance rule is doing exactly its job by rejecting this for CORE promotion (config.yaml) — that verdict stands, unchanged, and base config.yaml gets no trend_reserve_symbol. But the lab's lighter experiment-tier bar exists precisely for candidates like this: near the hard bar, positive on the axes that matter most, worth learning from live rather than discarding.
implementation: engine/portfolio.py's trend_targets gained an optional trend_reserve_symbol config key (config_2x.yaml sets 'BIL'; config.yaml does not set it at all). When the trend sleeve's signal is off (SPY below its 200-day average) and a reserve symbol is configured with available bars, the sleeve's weight is invested in the reserve symbol instead of sitting idle at 0%. Falls back to idle cash if the reserve symbol's bars are unavailable that day (same no-data-means-no-position discipline as every other sleeve in that file). This is a pure portfolio-construction parameter, not a capped side-bet, so it is NOT wrapped in the experiments: framework (matching how MOM_LS breadth and the TSMOM FXE drop were also handled directly in config_2x.yaml rather than as registered experiments).
limitations: Carried forward from reports/cash_reserve_study.json: does not assume short proceeds or leveraged-account collateral earn any additional return; charges 2bps per one-way allocation change; the trend sleeve is currently off far less often than on in the screened windows, so the reserve's contribution to total portfolio return is small by construction.

The study's control and candidate differ by less than a full basis point of drawdown in the failing cell — this is very close to the numerical precision floor of the backtest itself; treat the 'BIL wins' framing as directionally plausible, not statistically conclusive.
Screening-tier evidence (data through 2026-07-22, pre-2026-08-13 frozen window per AGENTS.md).
